correctness.rationale: The domain and strict interval-inclusion relation are explicitly defined and agree with positive roots of A_n. Quantifier-rank-three chain sentences separate parameters 1,...,7. For each 1<=n<=26 a complete three-round type recursion enumerates every ordered triple, with all equality and directed order atoms and recursive extension sets. The standalone C++17 run yields distinct types at n=1,...,7 and a single type for n=7,...,26; an independently structured Python recursion agrees through n=12. Separately, a three-round interval-endpoint gap argument maintains ordered endpoints with thresholds t_0=0, t_{r+1}=3t_r+2, giving equivalence for n,m>=26. Together these prove all quantified pairs, not just the tested range. Outputs were replayed from the packaged code and matched byte-for-byte. The theory-type recursion and gap-splitting lemma are reconstructed in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The family is the classical positive-root poset of every finite root system of type A_n, with unbounded root count, width and height. Quantifier rank three has a well-motivated finite-model-theoretic invariant: exactly which ranks remain distinguishable and the smallest uniform representative. The sharp answer seven and 28-root bound are not implied by the generic two-endpoint 26-point game argument or the numerical counts of root-poset edges, ideals or antichains. The result identifies a nontrivial stabilization phenomenon for a standard algebraic-combinatorial family; its modest scope and computation-assisted intermediate interval are fully disclosed.
